questions.q: Which opener fits: 'Through the columns of your esteemed daily, I wish to draw attention to…' or 'Hey Editor, your city is falling apart!'
questions.a: The first — public-formal register. The second is rant-register; letters to editors persuade through facts, not volume.

questions.q: A body reads 'The traffic is very bad and everyone is angry. Something must be done!!!' — what's missing?
questions.a: Facts (which road, what delay, what incidents), impact detail, and a specific suggestion — plus the exclamations must go. A wrong answer 'nothing' shows the student can't audit for content-completeness.

questions.q: Which close pairs correctly with 'To the Editor'?
questions.a: 'Yours sincerely' — the editor is a named-role recipient; 'faithfully' is for Dear Sir/Madam-unnamed pairs. Boards accept sincerely here.

questions.q: A letter to the editor is a formal letter with a public voice: full skeleton, then a body that states a civic issue with facts, its impact, and a ______ suggestion — through the columns of the paper, not to the editor personally.

Fill in the blank: A letter to the editor is a formal letter with a public voice: full skeleton, then a body that states a civic issue with facts, its impact, and a ______ suggestion — through the columns of the paper, not to the editor personally.

Fill in the blank: The three-beat body: (1) state the issue with specifics — 'the broken pavement on Mall Road has caused three falls this month'; (2) show impact on the public; (3) ______ a concrete fix or appeal to authorities.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes a letter-to-editor with correct formal skeleton, fact-based issue statement, impact paragraph, and a specific constructive suggestion — in measured public register.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The three-beat body: (1) state the issue with specifics — 'the broken pavement on Mall Road has caused three falls this month'; (2) show impact on the public; (3) suggest a concrete fix or appeal to ______.
